title: Simulated Traffic Runner: PRD + Operational Playbook for Cost & Fidelity Experiments
author: Maya Patel
content:
Summary:

This document defines the Product Requirements and an operational playbook for the Simulated Traffic Runner (STR) — an internal sandbox service and toolkit for generating realistic, parameterized request traffic to Redwood inference stacks (hosted, dedicated, private) to 1) estimate end-to-end cost impact for a given workload and configuration, 2) measure fidelity/latency tradeoffs across model variants and quantization profiles, and 3) produce repeatable datasets for regression/eval jobs.

Goal statement:

- Provide teams (product, solutions, SRE, research) a self-serve runner to mimic customer traffic patterns at configurable scale and fidelity.
- Produce reproducible cost/time/fidelity reports that feed into packaging decisions, pricing experiments, and rollout gating.

Non-goals:

- STR is not a load testing tool for breaking production limits; do not use it for destructive stress tests against live customer instances.
- STR will not replace the dedicated benchmarking harness used by serving-runtime for kernel microbenchmarks.

Key use-cases:

1) Pricing experiments: correlate token-level unit costs with request mix and batching policy to simulate credit consumption under hypothetical customer configurations.
2) Fidelity regression checks: run known prompt-sets across model/quantization matrix to detect quality regressions before rollouts.
3) Hosted→Dedicated migration planning: simulate tenant traffic to estimate required reserved capacity and expected 95th percentile latency.
4) E2E onboarding sandbox for enterprise trials: provide customers and SEs an isolated runner that demonstrates expected economics.

User personas and roles:

- Product Manager (owner): creates experiments, interprets reports, decides packaging changes.
- Solutions Engineer: configures simulation templates for a customer's traffic profile.
- SRE/Capacity Planner: uses STR outputs to size Dedicated commitments.
- Research/Applied ML: runs fidelity regression sweeps across quantization profiles.

Top-level success metrics (first 6 months):

- 30+ simulation runs executed per month by internal teams.
- Pricing experiment mean absolute error (MAE) vs observed bills <= 7% for Hosted API workloads.
- Fidelity regression false-positive rate < 3% against curated prompt-sets.

Functional requirements (MUST / SHOULD / MAY):

MUST:
- STR must support generating request streams that parameterize: request types (generation, chat, embeddings), prompt length distribution, token generation length distribution, context prefix reuse rate (to exercise KV cache), and concurrency patterns.
- STR must emit per-request telemetry compatible with Redwood Console ingest: route_id, model_variant, seq_len_in, seq_len_out, batch_id, latency_ms, token_count, success/error code.
- STR must produce a single-run report summarizing: total tokens, estimated cost (using pricing function), p50/p90/p95 latency, throughput (tokens/s), and fidelity deltas for provided prompt-sets.
- STR must integrate with Optimize recommendations to optionally apply suggested batching/quantization profiles and report comparative delta.

SHOULD:
- STR should be able to replay real anonymized tenant traces sanitized for PII and privacy.
- STR should provide experiment templates for common SaaS patterns: low-latency chat, high-throughput embeddings, large-document summarization.
- STR should support per-run tagging and metadata to map runs to quarterly roadmap/epic IDs.

MAY:
- STR may provide a lightweight UI in Console for configuring and launching experiments; initial rollout can be CLI-only.
- STR may expose a simulator mode (local only) which runs against a mocked runtime to measure compute-bound metrics without consuming production capacity.

API contract (example):

POST /v1/str/runs
Content-Type: application/json
Body (example):
{
  "template": "saas-chat-low-latency",
  "duration_minutes": 30,
  "concurrency": 50,
  "model_matrix": ["gptx-16k", "gptx-quant-8"],
  "kv_cache_reuse_pct": 60,
  "report_backends": ["console-reports", "s3://prod-str-results/"]
}

The response includes a run_id and status endpoint /v1/str/runs/{run_id} which returns run metadata and links to artifacts.

Experiment template table (canonical templates shipped with STR):

| template_name | primary_workload | concurrency | seq_len_in (avg) | seq_len_out (avg) | intent | notes |
| saas-chat-low-latency | chat | 10–100 | 32 | 64 | low-latency dialog | targets p95 < 300ms on hosted tier |
| embeddings-batch-throughput | embeddings | 50–500 | 512 | 0 | high-throughput vectorization | exercises batching and prefetch |
| long-doc-summarization | generation | 5–30 | 2048 | 512 | long-context summarization | stress KV cache and attention |

Operational telemetry and outputs:

- Per-request logs (structured JSON) stored to STR run bucket.
- Aggregated CSV and JSON summaries with histogram buckets for latency and token counts.
- Fidelity reports: per-prompt BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity deltas vs baseline.
- Cost estimation: line-item breakdown by model variant, tokens-in/tokens-out, and infra-surcharge (if dedicated).

SLOs and safety thresholds for STR runs:

- Default max concurrency per hosted-region test: 2x production per-tenant p95 concurrency to avoid cross-customer impact.
- STR runs that exceed 120% of observed per-region capacity must be flagged and require SRE approval before the run continues.
- Any run that generates > 5% error rate over 5 minutes triggers automatic throttling to preserve downstream services.

Security and privacy considerations:

- STR will never accept raw customer PII for replay unless explicitly approved and stored only in restricted buckets with KMS encryption.
- All run artifacts default to internal confidentiality; exports for customers require a documented data-sharing agreement.

Rollout plan and milestones (quarterly roadmap):

1) Q4 2026 — Alpha (internal CLI): basic templates, hosted-only, Console report link, required telemetry. Owner: Product + Eng (Optimize).
2) Q1 2027 — Beta (UI integration, Dedicated simulation): SRE gating controls, dedicated cost modeling, and sanitized trace replay. Owner: Product + Eng-SRE.
3) Q2 2027 — GA (Enterprise self-serve + guided templates): integrate with sales onboarding flow and legal-approved export. Owner: Product + Go-to-market.

Rollout checklist for each milestone:

1. Documentation published (this PRD + how-tos).
2. Internal training session for SEs and SREs.
3. Tagging and telemetry schema registered with Console.
4. Cost estimator calibration run vs 10 historical customer billing windows (MAE target <= 7%).

Runbook: launching an official STR experiment (for Solutions Engineers)

1. Select template or supply a custom load spec.
2. Validate model_matrix includes fallback variants.
3. Use dry-run mode (5 minutes, 1 concurrency) to validate telemetry mapping.
4. Schedule a 30-minute run, add reviewers (product + SRE).
5. Monitor /v1/str/runs/{run_id}/status for steady-state; abort if errors > 5% for sustained 2 minutes.

Post-run activities:

- STR generates automatic summary and emails stakeholders with links.
- For pricing experiments, attach run artifact to the pricing experiment issue and tag as "canonical" if representative.
- For fidelity regression runs, failure triggers an auto-create of a triage issue in regression-triage with links to per-prompt diffs.

Ownership and contacts:

- Product owner: Maya Patel (product)
- Engineering owners: Leo Hsu (eng-platform), Renata Gomes (eng-serving-runtime)
- SRE contact: Julian Park (eng-sre)

Open questions and decisions needed:

- Q1: Should STR calculate cost using the same on-the-book pricing engine or use a simplified estimator for speed? Recommendation: start with pricing engine but provide a fast-path estimator for iterative experiments.
- Q2: Level of Console UI investment at Beta. Minimum viable: link to run results; stretch: integrated wizard.

Appendix: sample cost estimation pseudocode

// simplified per-token cost estimator
function estimateCost(tokens_in, tokens_out, model_variant) {
  base_rate = Pricing.getRateFor(model_variant); // $ / 1000 tokens
  infra_surcharge = isDedicated(model_variant) ? 0.12 : 0.0; // example fraction
  return (tokens_in + tokens_out) / 1000 * base_rate * (1 + infra_surcharge);
}

Appendix: CLI example

redwood-str run --template saas-chat-low-latency --duration 30m --concurrency 50 --models gptx-16k,gptx-quant-8 --report s3://prod-str-results/my-run-20260928

Related artifacts to create after approval:

- 'STR run result schema' (telemetry table registration)
- 'Console STR summary card' design spec
- 'Customer-facing STR export playbook' (legal-approved templates)

Notes on uniqueness and relation to existing docs:

This PRD + playbook focuses specifically on an operational sandbox runner that bridges product experimentation (pricing, fidelity), capacity planning, and sales trials. It complements existing offline cost-estimator SDK and the Optimize cost-simulator by providing an execution harness that drives the runtime end-to-end under configurable traffic patterns.
